note: Table 6-7 of the W65C816S data sheet, which prints all eight output lines for every cycle of every addressing mode: vector pull, memory lock, the two address qualifiers, the address bus, what is on the data bus and the read write line. Nothing else here states the sixteen bit part's bus behaviour at rung one, so this is what its timing is held to when no recording is on the machine.
readHow: All seven pages read as printed. The extracted text is well aligned here, unlike the opcode matrix two pages earlier, so it was parsed and then checked row by row against the pages rather than trusted on its own.

notes.1: Add 1 byte (for immediate only) for M=0 or X=0 (i.e. 16-bit data), add 1 cycle for M=0 or X=0. REP, SEP are always 3 cycle instructions and VPA is low during the third cycle. The address bus is PC+1 during the third cycle.
notes.2: Add 1 cycle for direct register low (DL) not equal 0.
notes.3: Special case for aborting instruction. This is the last cycle which may be aborted or the Status, PBR or DBR registers will be updated.
notes.4: Add 1 cycle for indexing across page boundaries, or write, or X=0. When X=1 or in the emulation mode, this cycle contains invalid addresses.
notes.5: Add 1 cycle if branch is taken.
notes.6: Add 1 cycle if branch is taken across page boundaries in 6502 emulation mode (E=1).
notes.9: Wait at cycle 2 for 2 cycles after NMIB or IRQB active input.
notes.11: BRK bit 4 equals 0 in Emulation mode.
notes.13: Some OpCodes shown are compatible only with the W65C816S.
notes.14: VDA and VPA are not valid outputs on the W65C02S but are valid on the W65C816S.
notes.15: The PBR is only applicable to the W65C816S.
notes.17: In the emulation mode, during a R-M-W instruction the RWB is low during both write and modify cycles.

printingSlips.note: Cells where the page prints something the rest of the table spells differently. None changes what the row means, and all are kept under asPrinted so a reader holding the page can see why the record does not match it character for character.

kinds.PBR-PC+1: A hyphen where every other row of the table uses a comma, on group 2a.
kinds.PBR,NEWPC: No space, where the neighbouring rows print New PC, on group 1c.
kinds.Date High: A typo for Data High, on group 6b.
kinds.OP Code: A space, where every other row prints OpCode, on group 9b.
kinds.0.S-3: A full stop where the bank separator should be, on group 22j.
kinds.0,D+D0+1: A digit zero where the direct offset uses a letter O, on group 15.

disagreements.note: Nine of the two hundred and sixty-six rows a run reaches do not match what the part does. They fall into two classes, and neither is a defect in this model: the recorded cycles agree with the model on all nine.

widthDependentAddress.what: Each of these is the row directly after a lettered row that only exists when the register is sixteen bits, and each carries the address that only that longer form produces. With an eight bit register the part is one byte lower.
widthDependentAddress.why: The four read-modify-write groups put their modify cycle on the last byte read, which is AA+1 in the wide form and AA in the narrow one, and the table prints only AA+1. The push does the same: it writes at S in the narrow form and at S then S-1 in the wide one, and the table prints only S-1. The four modify cycles come out a byte higher and the push a byte lower, because the stack grows downward and everything else grows up.
widthDependentAddress.consequence: The table has no eight bit form of these rows, so a reader building a narrow register model from it puts the modify cycle and the push one byte too low.

qualifierOnAnIndexedIndirectJump.what: The two bytes of the new program counter. The table marks them a valid program address; the part marks them a valid data address.
qualifierOnAnIndexedIndirectJump.why: The table is not consistent with itself here. Group 3b is the same operation through a pointer in bank zero and its equivalent cycles are marked a data address. The two groups differ only in which bank holds the pointer.
qualifierOnAnIndexedIndirectJump.settledBy: Nothing here. It is recorded in divergences.json with what a real part would answer.
